info.title: RF backend API
info.description: HTTP surface for the Rust RF backend. Frontend calls go via Next.js route handlers at `/api/v2/*`, which bridge the Supabase session cookie to a bearer JWT before forwarding here.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size. Clamped to 200 server-side; defaults to 50 when omitted.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Zero-based offset from the newest entry.

404.description: Row not found or hidden by RLS

requestBody.description: CSV with required columns material_type, width, length, thickness and optional color, location, date_received, supplier, cost_per_sqft, notes. Header row is case-insensitive; whitespace → underscore.

400.description: CSV missing required columns or empty

200.description: Material-supplier rows with embedded material_type + supplier
All material types, ordered by name

404.description: Row not found or hidden by RLS

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: ILIKE sweep across material_type / color / location / supplier / notes.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of rows to return. Clamped server-side to 200.

200.description: Roll-count growth percentage, last-7d vs previous-7d
Count of material types below their min_stock_alert threshold

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: When set, only return suppliers matching the given active flag.

parameters.name: preferred
parameters.description: When set, only return suppliers matching the given preferred flag.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: ILIKE search across name / contact_person / email / city.

409.description: Blocked — material_supplier rows reference this supplier

400.description: subtotal must be a finite non-negative number

500.description: TAX_PROXY_BASE not configured or downstream failure

400.description: Validation failed (empty items, bad quantity, etc.)

409.description: Invalid transition. Body is `{ code: "INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION" | "RECEIVED_REQUIRES_RECEIVE_FLOW", details: { allowedTargets: [...] } }`. Received is only reachable via /api/v2/po/{id}/receive (Task 5).

201.description: Bulk PO created (1 PO, N line items)

409.description: RULE_NOT_FOUND, RULE_INACTIVE, SUPPLIER_NOT_FOUND, CHECK_VIOLATION, or FK_VIOLATION_PARENT_MISSING (transactional — any failure rolls back the entire bulk PO)

201.description: All N items succeeded; response is an ordered array of N receipts. IMPORTANT: the handler is NOT transactional across items — each input runs its own RPC and commits independently. A mid-batch failure returns 4xx/5xx and earlier successes persist in the DB but are NOT returned in the response body. Clients should refetch the PO list (or retry just the failing items) after a partial-batch error rather than trust the current response body on failure.

400.description: Validation failed (empty items / negative quantity / etc.)

409.description: RULE_NOT_FOUND, RULE_INACTIVE, SUPPLIER_NOT_FOUND, DUPLICATE_RULE_IDS, CHECK_VIOLATION, or FK_VIOLATION_PARENT_MISSING. Earlier items in the batch may have committed (see 201 notes).

parameters.name: include_pending
parameters.description:
Default `false` — rules with at least one non-draft PO
line item are excluded. Set to `true` to show them anyway
(the UI's "review pending" affordance).

409.description: RULE_NOT_FOUND, RULE_INACTIVE, SUPPLIER_NOT_FOUND, DUPLICATE_RULE_IDS, CHECK_VIOLATION, or FK_VIOLATION_PARENT_MISSING

CreateMaterialTypeBody.description:
Request body for POST — mandatory `name`, everything else
optional. The handler validates constraints through the use
case; the adapter maps a DB unique violation to a stable
`DUPLICATE_NAME` conflict code.

CreatePurchaseOrderBody.description: Body for POST. `status` defaults to `draft` server-side if omitted.

CreateRollBody.description:
Create body. Caller sends `material_type_id`; the server looks
up the corresponding name. Any `material_type` string in the
body is ignored.

CutHistoryDto.description:
Response DTO — thin wrapper over the domain entry. Separated from
`CutHistoryEntry` so the HTTP contract can evolve independently
of domain schema. Today the mapping is 1:1; renaming / derived
fields will land here first when we start splitting concerns.

ImportRollRowBody.description:
Matches `CsvImportRow` on the wire. `material_type_id` is
optional and null-safe — the dedicated review page fills it
when the row matches an existing material, and leaves it null
when the user typed a new name.

percentage.description: Percentage growth vs. the prior 7 days.

oneOf.description:
The embedded material_types row, present on list/get, absent
on create/update response (PostgREST Prefer:
return=representation doesn't include embeds).

MaterialTypeDto.description:
Response DTO — mirrors the domain struct 1:1 today. Separated
from `MaterialType` so the HTTP contract can evolve without
reaching into the domain type.

PurchaseOrderDto.description:
Response DTO — mirrors the domain struct. Separate so the HTTP
surface can diverge from the domain without a domain change.

ReceiveReceiptDto.description:
Response DTO — JSON representation of `ReceiveReceipt`. Kept
separate so the HTTP shape can evolve without touching the
use-case struct.

TaxPreviewDto.description:
Response shape — mirrors the TS service's `TaxCalculation` minus
the redundant `subtotal` / `total` fields (the client already has
those). `tax_level` is one of `"state"`, `"city"`, `"zip_code"`,
`"default"`, `"exempt"`, `"override"`, or `"api"`; `tax_name`
is the human-readable label the PO dialog shows (`"Texas State"`,
`"Tax Exempt"`, `"Supplier Override Rate"`, etc.). Both are
passed through verbatim — treated as opaque at this layer.

UpdateMaterialTypeBody.description:
Request body for PUT. Every field is optional so the HTTP surface
can evolve to PATCH semantics later without breaking callers —
for now, the UI always sends a full replacement. Nullable fields
use `Option<Option<T>>` via `serde_with`-style manual handling:
`null` in JSON explicitly clears the column, omitted means leave
as-is.

To keep the DTO simple we expose the fields as plain `Option<T>`
here. Semantics: present-and-non-null replaces the column,
present-and-null is the same as omitting (the UI today never
needs to explicitly null a column). If that distinction matters
later we'll promote to `Option<Option<T>>` + a custom visitor.

UpdatePurchaseOrderBody.description:
Body for PUT — status is NOT on this type. Status changes go
through `PUT /api/v2/po/{id}/status` (Task 3), which enforces the
state machine + blocks `received` from the generic path.

UpdatePurchaseOrderStatusBody.description:
`PUT /api/v2/po/{id}/status` body. `status` is the lowercase
string variant (`draft` / `pending` / `approved` / `ordered` /
`cancelled`). `received` is accepted on the wire but rejected
in the use case with a 409 — we deliberately don't drop it at
parse time so the error carries the structured
`allowedTargets` payload the UI consumes.

UpdateSupplierBody.description:
Update body — all fields optional. Single-level `Option<T>` for
simplicity; explicit null-ing of columns isn't something the UI
needs today. When it does, promote to Option<Option<T>>.

supabase_jwt.description: Supabase-issued RS256 JWT. Forwarded to PostgREST so RLS scopes rows to the caller.
